Close michaelIsADullGuy's Diary 南京新街口地块精细化更新日志 Posted by michaelIsADullGuy on 29 May 2026 in Chinese (China) (‪中文(中国大陆)‬) . 前言 新街口作为南京乃至华东地区最重要的商业核心之一，其 OSM 数据长期存在建筑轮廓粗糙、地下空间缺失、路径拓扑混乱等问题。为此，我启动了一项针对新街口地块的系统性精细化更新计划，并在此记录操作步骤与我所制定的制图标准，供社区参考与讨论。 一、建筑物轮廓与属性细化 所有建筑物的轮廓均参照最新卫星影像与实地核查进行重新描绘或修正，具体标准如下： 轮廓贴合建筑基底，避免过度简化或偏移； 补充 building:levels 、 height 、 name 、 start_date 等属性； 对于综合体建筑（如德基广场、金鹰国际），区分裙楼与塔楼，分别以 building 、 building:part 进行三维建模。 二、地下商业空间的划定 新街口地铁站（地铁1号线×2号线换乘）向四周延伸出大量地下通道，直接连通周边各大商场的负一层。凡与地铁站地下通道 直接联通 的商场负一层空间，均按以下标准标注为地下建筑区域： 使用 location=underground 或 layer=-1 标记相关区域； 地下商业区域的范围多边形参照实际通道出入口与商业空间边界绘制； 与地铁站直接相连的通道本身，以 tunnel=yes + layer=-1 的 highway=footway 表示； 暂不确定是否联通的区域，暂以 fixme=需核实地下联通情况 标注，留待后续实地核查。 目前已完成地下空间划定的区域包括： 新街口百货商店 B1、金陵中环 B1 待补充区域： 金鹰国际购物中心 B1、德基广场 B1、中央商场 B1、南京国际金融中心 B1 等。 三、路径拓扑标准 这是本次更新中最容易出错的部分。为确保路网拓扑的清洁与导航规划的准确性，我制定了以下强制性规则： 3.1 各类道路不得混接 在主要路口， 行人路径（ highway=footway/pedestrian ）、自行车道（ highway=cycleway ）、机动车道（ highway=primary 等） 三者之间，原则上不建议建立直接连接节点，除非现实中存在明确的路权交汇点（如行人过街横道节点）。 3.2 跨图层要素禁止连接 任何两个 不属于同一 layer 值 的路径要素， 不得出现共享连接节点 ，以下情况除外： 允许连接的要素 说明 highway=steps 阶梯，连接不同楼层/层级 含 conveying=yes 的 highway=footway 自动扶梯 highway=elevator 电梯 除上述垂直交通要素外，地面路径与地下路径 一律不得出现连接点 。 此规则同样适用于在导航计算中看似”无害”的连接（例如建筑物轮廓与步行道路相切）。只要两个要素不属于同一图层，路径要素与非路径要素之间同样须保持几何上的独立性，仅在视觉上相邻即可。同一图层内的要素按正常规则连接，不受此限制。 如有异议或建议，欢迎在变更集评论或讨论页留言。 Happy mapping! 🗺️ Discussion Leave a comment Log in to leave a comment

pages.text: Michelangelo (1475 - 1564) | National Gallery, London Skip to main content Painter, on panel and in fresco , sculptor and architect, writer of sonnets, Michelangelo Buonarroti was the first artist recognised by contemporaries as a genius. Hero of the High Renaissance . He was the only artist of whom it was claimed in his lifetime that he surpassed Antiquity . He was born in Caprese in the 1470s and trained first as a painter with Ghirlandaio , and then as a sculptor under the patronage of Lorenzo de' Medici . In 1496, already known as sculptor, he went to Rome, where he carved the 'Pietà' for St Peter's. Back in Florence in 1501 he began work on many sculptural and painterly projects most of which were left unfinished in 1505, when he was summoned to Rome to begin work on a sculpted tomb for Pope Julius II, a project that dogged him until 1545. From 1508 to 1512 he painted the vault of the Sistine Chapel with scenes from the Old Testament, from the Creation to the Story of Noah. Immediately celebrated, the Sistine Chapel ceiling, with its innumerable figures in complex, twisting poses and its exuberant use of colour, is the chief source of the Mannerist style. But nothing burdened him more than the tomb of Pope Julius II. “Moses" by Michelangelo Created between 1513 and 1516, this sculpture became the centerpiece of Pope Julius II’s tomb when it was installed in 1545. Anna Serrano/Fototeca 9x12 By Eloi de Tera Published November 16, 2026 The warm torpor of summer still lingered in the long afternoons of September 1534, when momentous news reached Florence. Giulio de’ Medici, Pope Clement VII, had died on the 25th of that month, after allegedly eating poisonous mushrooms. The tomb of Giuliano de’ Medici, with figures “Night” and “Day,” was designed and sculpted by Michelangelo. Guido Cozzi/Fototeca 9x12 At the time, within the so-called New Sacristy of the Basilica of San Lorenzo in Florence (an architectural space conceived as a mausoleum for the Medici family), scaffolding was being erected under the watchful eye of Michelangelo Buonarroti. The artist, known to the world today as Michelangelo, was nearly 60 years old and had been commissioned to design the sacristy, which would mirror Filippo Brunelleschi’s Old Sacristy. But events overtook him. A few days earlier, he had left Florence for Rome, where he arrived on September 23, just two days before the pope’s death. pages.description: While restoring the Sistine Chapel, researchers discovered wavy groupings of brushstrokes which indicated that the artist used the special brushes to create a distinct crosshatching pattern
pages.text: Michelangelo Used These Custom, Multi-Headed Brushes While Painting 'The Last Judgment' to Replicate His Intricate Sculpting Techniques Skip to main content Detail showing the hair of one of the figures around Christ in The Last Judgment , as example of the use of a multi-tipped brush Governatorato SCV – Direzione dei Musei e dei Beni Culturali This spring, the Vatican restored the Sistine Chapel for the first time in 30 years. Restorers worked for three months to remove layers of calcium lactate—a whitish salt from the dried sweat from millions of visitors and the plaster in the walls—that had settled onto Michelangelo ’s immaculate 16th-century murals. As experts climbed temporary scaffolding and applied distilled water and absorbent Japanese paper to clean away the grime, they got a rare, close-up view of Michelangelo’s vivid masterpieces. They noticed something unique about The Last Judgment , the massive mural located behind the chapel’s altar, as its original colors emerged. Michelangelo had painted with wavy brushstrokes that appeared to have moved in synchronization. “I initially saw that Michelangelo painted with parallel strokes, often perpendicular to each to give a cross-hatching effect,” Paolo Violini , the Vatican’s chief restorer, tells the London Times ’ Tom Kington. “Then I saw that when a stroke wobbled slightly, other strokes parallel to it had an identical wobble. pages.text: Michelangelo | The Entombment (or Christ being carried to his Tomb) | NG790 | National Gallery, London Skip to main content Michelangelo, 'The Entombment (or Christ being carried to his Tomb)', about 1500-1 The Entombment (or Christ being carried to his Tomb) Michelangelo Room 2 Framed About the work Overview In-depth Audio description Overview This is one of perhaps only three surviving panel paintings by the great Florentine artist Michelangelo. It shows Christ’s body being carried to his tomb. It was probably made for a funerary chapel in the church of S. Agostino, Rome – commissioned in 1500 and left unfinished when Michelangelo returned to Florence the following year. Saint John the Evangelist may be the figure on the left carrying Christ’s body on strips of winding cloth helped by one of the Three Marys. They carry him up a staircase to his tomb in the rocks. The man behind Christ is either Joseph of Arimathea or Nicodemus. Another of the Three Marys, possibly Mary Magdalene, sits on the ground. The space left empty on the right was probably intended for the kneeling figure of the Virgin Mary. The other female figure on the right is probably another of the Three Marys, Mary Salome. In-depth This unfinished painting shows Christ’s body being carried to his tomb in the rocks behind him. It is one of only three known surviving panel paintings by the great Florentine artist Michelangelo – the others are The Virgin and Child with Saint John and Angels (‘The Manchester Madonna’) and the Doni Tondo (Uffizi, Florence). pages.text: Michigan's Isle Royale National Park Is a camper's paradise | National Geographic National Geographic Traveller (UK) content straight to your inbox — sign up for our newsletter here TRAVEL Everything you should know about Isle Royale National Park Michigan’s remote and rugged Lake Superior archipelago—which encompasses nearly 450 islands—is a true Northwoods escape, ideal for hikers, wildlife lovers, and stargazers. In western Lake Superior, Isle Royale National Park is an archipelago comprised of over 400 smaller islands and rocky islets, including Siksiwit Island, Chippewa Harbor Islands, and Mott Island, the park’s summer headquarters on the south side of Rock Harbor Channel. Aaron Black-Schmidt, Tandem Stock By Amy S. Eckert Last updated March 31, 2026 • 13 min read Isle Royale National Park offers an unforgettable Lake Superior wilderness escape in Michigan . Despite its name, Isle Royale encompasses not merely its namesake island, but an archipelago of nearly 450 islands located 14 miles (22.5 km) from the nearest mainland. Once in the park, you’ll discover a landscape of rocky shoreline and basalt ridges covered with sugar maple, birch, and evergreen forest. The woods are carpeted with delicate wildflowers like bluebells, Canada Mayflowers, and lady’s slippers, and in late summer, you can harvest thimbleberries for snacking. If you’re lucky, you may spot moose, wolves, and aquatic birds along the park’s 165 miles (265 km) of hiking trails. A better understanding of these complex microbial communities would help us harness them for applications to human and animal health, agriculture and food safety, water treatment, manufacturing, renewable energy, and the detection of biological threats. The microloan program provides loans up to $50,000 to help small businesses and certain not-for-profit childcare centers start up and expand. The average microloan is about $13,000. SBA provides funds to specially designated intermediary lenders, which are nonprofit community-based organizations with experience in lending as well as management and technical assistance. These intermediaries administer the Microloan program for eligible borrowers. Am I eligible? To be eligible for a microloan, businesses must: Not be a type of ineligible business Be an operating business Operate for profit Be located in the U.S. Be small under SBA size requirements How do I use a microloan? Microloans can be used for a variety of purposes that help small businesses expand. Use them when you need less than $50,000 to start and/or grow your small business. How to roll back Microsoft Edge to a previous version Feedback Summarize this article for me This article describes how to roll back to a previous version of Microsoft Edge using the rollback feature. To learn more about this feature, watch Video: Microsoft Edge version rollback . Introduction to rollback Rollback lets you replace your Microsoft Edge browser version with an earlier version. This feature is designed to be a safety net for enterprises deploying Microsoft Edge. It provides a way to troubleshoot issues with Microsoft Edge. The benefits of rollback are the ability to revert to previous browser version easily and quickly. Rollback reduces the potential impact that a Microsoft Edge issue has on business operations. Before you begin It's important to understand how the rollback feature is installed in a Microsoft Edge environment. You can deploy rollback using two different methods: manually with an MSI or by using Microsoft Edge update and Group Policy. We also encourage using a selection of Group Policies for a smoother deployment. A critical Microsoft outage lasting more than 22 hours has raised questions about how heavily vital services rely on a handful of major tech firms. The disruption, which affected Microsoft 365 services such as Outlook, was caused by routine automated checks that took some servers offline, overloading the remaining ones with traffic. The recovery took nearly a full day while engineers gradually restored services, highlighting how embedded the tech giant's services are in modern society. Flora Hamilton, executive director of the Small Business Charter, said the outage was a "stark reminder" of how much firms "rely on digital systems" - like Microsoft Outlook - "to keep their operations running". "For many small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), access to email is fundamental to everything from communicating with customers and suppliers to generating income," she said. The disruption was not just confined to businesses, but also affected organisations and public institutions around the world. Around 430 million people globally use Microsoft 365, and issues were reported across more than 70 countries. A medida que los flujos migratorios se vuelven más complejos – en particular debido al aumento de los desplazamientos forzosos y de los movimientos migratorios mixtos –, la protección de los trabajadores migrantes y refugiados sigue siendo un elemento central del mandato de la OIT, consagrado en el preámbulo de su Constitución desde 1919. La mayor parte de la migración internacional está motivada por la búsqueda de trabajo decente y de medios de vida dignos. Si bien la migración puede brindar mejores salarios y oportunidades para el desarrollo de competencias, muchos trabajadores migrantes siguen excluidos de las protecciones laborales y son vulnerables a la discriminación y la explotación. Para las poblaciones desplazadas, el acceso al trabajo decente es un elemento esencial de las soluciones de desarrollo sostenible, ya que permite a los refugiados participar activamente en las economías y sociedades de las comunidades de acogida y contribuir a ellas. Se necesita cooperación internacional para formular políticas que maximicen los beneficios de la migración laboral y proporcionen trabajo decente para todos. Buildings that look like the real thing Churches are built from their real outline. The game reads the shape of the building and finds the nave, the transepts and the choir, and each part gets its own roof that follows the shape. A square part that sticks out becomes the tower. A church mapped carefully as a cross shape now also looks like one at eye level. Mosques get a dome on a drum, pointed windows and a minaret. They are recognised by religion=muslim , building=mosque or the name. Cemeteries ( landuse=cemetery ) are laid out with gravel paths, rows of graves in neutral shapes, low hedges and trees. Sidewalks now run along the whole street as one continuous strip. Short gaps are filled and corners join neatly. I’ve been building Wandering Around , a free browser game in which you can walk around any town or city on Earth. The game fetches the tiles around the player, decodes them in the browser, stitches buildings that are split across tile edges and turns everything back into OSM-style features with tags. Nimitz with his third Gold Star Chester William Nimitz Fleet Admiral, United States Navy Born: 1885 in Fredericksburg, Texas Died: 1966 in San Francisco Bay, California Buried: Golden Gate National Cemetery, San Bruno, California Significance: Admiral Nimitz was Commander in Chief, United States Pacific Fleet at the time of the Liberation of Guam and the attacks on Iwo Jima and Okinawa. After graduating from the Naval Academy in 1905, he served on various ships in the Pacific. On December 31, 1941 he assumed command of the Pacific Fleet. At the end of the war, his headquarters was at Fonte Plateau, now called Nimitz Hill, in Guam. In 1944 he was promoted to Fleet Admiral and served as Chief of Naval Operations. On September 2, 1945, Nimitz signed for the United States when Japan formally surrendered on board the Missouri in Tokyo Bay. pages.text: Military survivor benefits and life insurance | USAGov Skip to main content Military survivor benefits and life insurance Active duty, veterans, and retirees may be eligible to enroll in programs to provide for their survivors. Find out about military and veterans survivor benefits and life insurance. Military survivor benefits Eligibility for survivor benefits is generally based on the service history of a military service member. Learn about benefits for survivors of: Retired active duty service members and reservists Veterans who served during a qualifying wartime period Veterans who died from a service-connected injury or illness Survivor benefits for retirees As a military retiree, your pension payments end when you die. Retired active duty and reservists may enroll in an annuity program when they retire. These programs will give your survivors a portion of your pension for the rest of their lives. Active duty retirees can enroll in the Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) to provide for their survivors. Learn about the SBP , including: Program costs Benefits for your survivors Updates to your plan Retiring reservists can enroll in the Reserve Component Survivor Benefit Plan (RCSBP). Learn about the RCSBP , including: Eligibility Enrollment Changes to your plan Survivor benefits for wartime veterans A surviving spouse or child of a veteran who served during a qualifying wartime period may be eligible for the VA Survivors Pension . pages.text: Military tuition assistance | USAGov Skip to main content Military tuition assistance Service members, veterans, and their families may be able to get help paying for college or training programs. Learn about the benefit programs, including the GI Bill and more. Military branch scholarship programs Each branch of the military offers college scholarships to eligible students. They also pay for books and fees and provide stipends. Accepting this scholarship requires you to serve in the military. After college graduation, a graduate will begin a career as a commissioned officer. ROTC scholarships The Reserve Officer Training Corps (ROTC) is a scholarship program sponsored by the military. High school seniors, current college students, or enlisted service members can apply for an ROTC scholarship. Learn more about eligibility, participating campuses, and the application process for each branch of the military. Air Force ROTC Army ROTC Navy and Marine ROTC Coast Guard College Student Pre-Commissioning Initiative The Coast Guard offers scholarships through the College Student Pre-Commissioning Initiative (CSPI). The program pays school fees, a housing allowance, and salary. Learn how CSPI works, what schools participate in the program, and find a recruiter to apply. Education benefits for veterans and dependents GI Bill and other education benefits for veterans The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) offers the GI Bill, a benefit that helps veterans pay for college or job training. When discussing a child’s type 2 diabetes risk, parents prefer practical advice that is personalized and free of judgment. This mini-toolkit can support providers in helping families improve their health and prevent type 2 diabetes. Building healthy habits together Conversations about a child's type 2 diabetes risk can be difficult, but they are an important part of helping families stay healthy. Health care providers can make these discussions more effective by listening, showing respect, and avoiding blame or judgment. Parents want advice that recognizes they know their child best and provides simple, realistic steps they can take. Encouraging healthy habits for the whole family—such as drinking fewer sugary beverages, being more active together, and limiting screen time—can help families make lasting changes. This excerpt from the Baseball Traveler newsletter, presented by Circle K, is a mere taste of the smorgasbord of delights he offers every week. Read the full newsletter here , and subscribe to the newsletter here . To be alive is to ask the question, "What could’ve been?" How would things have turned out if, at a key moment, a different decision had been made? Minor League Baseball teams are not immune to this common source of agita. For every team identity, there are many others that were considered but ultimately rejected. Some of these forsaken names have been brought to life via "What Could’ve Been" promotions, in which teams spend an evening embracing a path not taken. Many others have been relegated to the dustbin of history, celebrated by no one, remembered by few. Let us now travel through the graveyard of rejected Minor League team names, primarily focused on identities briefly resurrected for a What Could've Been-style theme night. There are many more where these came from, and innumerable others we'll never know. Photograph: Matthew Stockman/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Mirra Andreeva throws her racket up in delight after her final victory. Photograph: Matthew Stockman/Getty Images WTA Finals Mirra Andreeva holds nerve against Svitolina to win WTA Finals for first time Andreeva seals 7-5, 6-3 victory to earn world No 2 ranking Russian dominates tournament without losing a set Tumaini Carayol Sun 15 Nov 2026 17.39 EST Last modified on Sun 15 Nov 2026 21.30 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Mirra Andreeva had put herself on the brink of securing another effortless, straightforward set in one of the biggest finals of her career when she momentarily balked. Serving for the first set at 5-4, Andreeva nervously opened the game with two dire double faults before spraying two further unforced errors to hand over the break. There have already been many times in Andreeva’s young career when similar sequences triggered epic, dramatic collapses, so prone the 19-year-old has been to losing her composure when things do not go her way. This time, she betrayed no negative emotions at all. Andreeva immediately retrieved the break and regained her momentum as she marched to a monumental victory, defeating Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to win the WTA Finals at Indian Wells for the first time.
